graph.title: Shelob Attacks (LEGO The Lord of the Rings 9470)
notes:
The booklet builds separate things: the Gollum ruin (pp.4-9), Shelob the spider (pp.11-36), and the Frodo and Sam minifigures (p.3). They are not physically fastened to each other. I added only contact edges, taken from the cover and p.38 display arrangement, so the graph is one component:
- Gollum rests on the ruin.
- The hook at the end of the spider's web string touches Frodo, who is wrapped in the web on the cover.
- Sam stands beside the ruin.
None of these are structural joins.

Ids b1-b28 are the ruin. b29-b72 are the spider's cephalothorax. b73-b115 are the abdomen. b116-b133 are the minifigures. b134-b135 are the pieces added to match the parts-page counts: one 281726 and the second 4211247. b69 is unused: the two side-pod assemblies of steps 16 and 17 are the 'sidepod' repeat.

The booklet's parts page prints the eight spider body hinge plates (the black, wavy 1x4 hinge plates used in steps 2, 4 and 5 of the body) as '74011'. That is not a valid element number, so I modelled them with the catalogue type lego-74230 (Hinge plate 1x4), coloured black. The element ID is therefore uncertain, and the parts-page count for '74011' will not match the graph.

281726 (black plate 2x2 with axle hole, x1 on the parts page) is not clearly identifiable in any step picture. I placed it on top of the pivot brick b54 as a bearing cap (b134), which is a guess. The second 4211247 (dark red plate, parts page x2) is likewise not located in any step. I placed it (b135) on the tan 2x8 plate b81. Both placements are guesses.

Each leg (8x) has 3 of the 4521427 hinge plates (matching the parts page count of 24), but only two are clearly visible in the steps. I added the third (d3) stacked on the 1x2 plate p2, which is a guess.

Stud and anti-stud joins use null ports. The catalogue gives each brick one stud port and one anti-stud port, standing for the whole surface, and many bricks carry several parts. Naming the port would reuse a single-use port. Named ports are used only for pins, holes, clips, bars, hinges, balls and axles.

Port-kind fixes from the first pass:
- The hook has a bar port.
- The pivot piece 4213374 has a ball port in the socket of b54, plus an axle-hole for the abdomen axle.
- The small cogs 4211506 are pin-hole parts on the pins of b70.
- Frodo's hair uses anti-stud.1.
- Minifig head, cape and torso are a stud/anti-stud stack.
- The torso hip is an anti-stud over the catalogue legs hip.
- Sam's torso hand.2 is a socket for the clear sack.
The two side pods (steps 16-17) are mirror copies. Their pin plates (4211881) plug into the side pin-holes of the two dark grey brackets b50 and b51, one each. This is inferred from small pictures.

Element IDs come from the inventory pages. Where the catalogue had no entry, or its port list was clearly wrong for the piece as used, I made new types. Stud placements (which piece sits on which) are best guesses from small step pictures. Ruin step 5 shows a small black cylinder in the 4210660 sub-assembly that I could not identify, so it is not modelled.
The string/hook, the two pulleys, the tan gear and the 24-tooth gear sit on the ribbed axle 4560177. The axle end.2 plugs into the pivot piece 4213374 on the head so the abdomen rotates (p.37).
Minifig assembly (p.3) is included: Frodo has hair, head, cape, torso, legs, sword and bowl. Sam has hair, head, cape, torso, legs, sword and the clear sack. Gollum has a body, two arms and the fish.

graph_initial.title: Shelob Attacks (LEGO The Lord of the Rings 9470)
notes: The booklet has two models: the Gollum ruin (pp.4-9, with Gollum/fish) and Shelob the spider (pp.11-36), plus the Frodo and Sam minifigures (p.3). All three are in this one graph.

Ids b1-b28 are the ruin. b29-b72 are the spider's cephalothorax. b73-b115 are the abdomen. b116-b133 are the minifigures. b69 is unused: the two side-pod assemblies of steps 16 and 17 are the 'sidepod' repeat.

Element IDs come from the inventory pages. Where the catalogue had no entry, or its port list was clearly wrong for the piece as used, I made new types. The remaining catalogue types are used with their catalogue port names, so a few port names are approximations. Examples are 4183043 and 4563477, which are shown as a hinge plate and a claw.

Stud/anti-stud joins are inferred from the small step pictures. Which stud a piece sits on is a best guess in several places, for example the back and front plates of the abdomen and the body step-5/6 stack. The overall assembly order and which piece sits on which is believed correct.

Each leg (8x) has these pieces:
- 4211190 plate 1x4, 2x 4183043 hinge plates, 4211151 plate 1x2, 2x 4521427 hinge plates, 4504376 slope, 4158848 ridged piece and 4563477 claw.
- The inventory counts 24x 4521427, which is three per leg, but only two are identifiable in the steps. The third per leg is not modelled (8 pieces unmodelled in total).
- Each leg's root piece (d1) is shown plugging onto the two studs of one of the eight 74011 hinge plates on the body (pp.19-20). Which hinge plate each copy uses is arranged via the attach overrides.

The two side pods (steps 16-17) are mirror copies. Their pin plates (4211881) are shown plugging into the side of the head. I connected both to the pin-hole of the dark grey 2x2 brick b54, but the real second attachment point may differ.

Ruin step 5 shows a small black cylinder inside the 4210660 sub-assembly. I could not identify it as a separate inventory element, so it is not modelled. The grey pin b7 is connected both to the 1x1 technic brick and to the 4210660 sub-assembly.

The string/hook (6010591, 6008602), the two pulleys (4521532) and the tan gear (4565452) sit on the ribbed axle 4560177. The axle also carries the 24-tooth gear 4211434 on its lower end. The axle's lower end plugs into the black pivot piece 4213374 on the head so the abdomen rotates (p.37). The axle also passes through the abdomen hull; no explicit edge is given for that.

Minifigure assembly (p.3) is included: Frodo has hair, head, cape, torso, legs, sword and bowl. Sam has hair, head, cape, torso, legs, sword and the clear sack (4248937). Gollum has a body, two arms and the fish.
The third Gollum pose in the booklet (rest on the ruin) is modelled as a contact edge only. The minifig hand ports are approximated with clip/bar kinds.
